# `nish/net/quic-frame`

The frames of QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000 §19) and RFC 9221's DATAGRAM, read from a decrypted packet payload and written into one, and the transport error codes a connection closes with (§20.1).

```ts
import { QuicFrame, quicParseFrame, quicPushAck, QUIC_FRAME_CRYPTO } from "nish/net/quic-frame";

const frame = new QuicFrame();                       // one per connection, reused
let at: i32 = 0;
while (at < toI32(payload.length)) {
  const error: i64 = quicParseFrame(frame, payload, at, toI32(payload.length));
  if (error !== 0) { … close the connection with `error` … }
  if (frame.type === QUIC_FRAME_CRYPTO) { … payload[frame.dataStart .. + frame.dataLength) … }
  at = frame.end;
}
```

<scalar-card title="quicPutAck" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputack">

Writes an ACK frame (§19.3) for the `rangeCount` pairs of `ranges`, each `[smallest, largest]`, from the highest down and not touching (each pair's largest at least two below the smallest of the pair before it), with `ackDelay` already scaled by this endpoint's exponent.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutConnectionClose" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputconnectionclose">

Writes a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (§19.19): with `application` false the transport form 0x1c, carrying `frameType`, the type of the frame that caused the error (0 when none did); with `application` true the 0x1d form, which has no frame type.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutCrypto" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputcrypto">

Writes a CRYPTO frame (§19.6) carrying `data[from .. from + length)` at stream offset `offset`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutDatagram" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputdatagram">

Writes a DATAGRAM frame with a Length (type 0x31, RFC 9221 §4) carrying `data[from .. from + length)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutNewConnectionId" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputnewconnectionid">

Writes a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame (§19.15) for the first `cidLength` bytes of `connectionId`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutPadding" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputpadding">

Writes `count` PADDING frames, zero bytes, into `buf[at .. at + count)`, clamped to `buf`, and answers the offset past them.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutPathData" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputpathdata">

Writes a PATH_CHALLENGE or PATH_RESPONSE frame carrying the eight bytes `data[from .. from + 8)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutStream" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputstream">

Writes a STREAM frame (§19.8) carrying `length` bytes of `data` on `streamId` at `offset`, with FIN when `fin`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutStreamError" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputstreamerror">

Writes a RESET_STREAM frame (§19.4) or, with `finalSize` at -1, a STOP_SENDING frame (§19.5).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutStreamValue" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputstreamvalue">

Writes a MAX_STREAM_DATA or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame: the stream ID and the limit.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="quicPutTypeOnly" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputtypeonly">

Writes a frame that is its type alone, PING or HANDSHAKE_DONE; -1 for another type or no room.

<scalar-card title="quicPutValue" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#quicputvalue">

Writes a frame of one varint after its type: MAX_DATA, MAX_STREAMS_BIDI, MAX_STREAMS_UNI, DATA_BLOCKED, STREAMS_BLOCKED_BIDI, STREAMS_BLOCKED_UNI or RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID.

</scalar-card>

The bytes a STREAM frame's header takes for `length` bytes of data on `streamId` at `offset`: the type, the stream ID, the offset when it is not zero, and the length, which `quicPutStream` always writes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="QuicFrame" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#quicframe">

One frame as `quicParseFrame` read it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-detail title="Coverage">

Every frame type of RFC 9000 is read, 0x00 to 0x1e, and RFC 9221's
DATAGRAM, 0x30 and 0x31, so a type outside those is the one parse error a
well-formed packet cannot produce. What
a frame *means* is `nish/net/quic`'s: this module checks only what §19 says
of the encoding itself, and answers the transport error the RFC names for
each break — `QUIC_ERROR_FRAME_ENCODING` for a truncated field, a length
past the packet, an ACK range below packet number zero, an offset past
2^62 − 1, a stream count past 2^60, an empty NEW_TOKEN, a connection ID
outside 1 to 20 bytes or a Retire Prior To above its own sequence number;
`QUIC_ERROR_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` for a frame type spelled in more bytes than
it needs (§12.4). Every read is bounds-checked against the window the caller
gives, so nothing a peer sends can make this module panic.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="No copy of the bulk">

A CRYPTO, STREAM or DATAGRAM frame's data, a
NEW_TOKEN's token, a PATH_CHALLENGE's eight bytes and a CONNECTION_CLOSE's
reason are left in the payload and described by `dataStart` and
`dataLength`, and a NEW_CONNECTION_ID's ID and token by windows of their
own, so a connection reassembles straight from the packet. One `QuicFrame`
is reused for every frame of every packet: `quicParseFrame` overwrites
every field it reads and resets the rest, and stores nothing but numbers,
so a payload made inside an arena block can be read inside it.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Writers">

They come in two forms. A `put` writer writes one frame into a
caller's buffer at an offset, before an end, and answers the offset past
it, or -1 with nothing written; a `push` writer appends one to an array
and answers whether it could, by growing the array and calling the `put`
form, so each frame has one encoder. Either refuses a value no varint
holds or a window outside the array given. Their inputs are this
endpoint's own, never a peer's. `quicFrameAllowed` is RFC 9000 §12.4's
table of which frames each packet type may carry.

</scalar-detail>

Written from RFC 9000 §12.4, §19 and §20 and RFC 9221 §4, in this module's own structure;
nothing here is ported from another implementation. Private names carry the
`quicFrame` prefix because a `std/` module's private functions share the
importing program's flat symbol namespace (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

## quicAckSize

The size of the ACK frame `quicPutAck` writes for these ranges, or 0 when
it would refuse them: no ranges, ranges out of order or touching, a pair
the array does not hold, or a value no varint holds.

```ts
function quicAckSize(
  ranges: i64[],
  rangeCount: i32,
  ackDelay: i64,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="ranges" type="i64[]" required>

Packet number pairs laid out flat, `[smallest, largest]` for each range, highest range first.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="rangeCount" type="i32" required>

How many pairs to read from the front of `ranges`; the rest of the array is ignored.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ackDelay" type="i64" required>

The ACK Delay field, already scaled by this endpoint's `ack_delay_exponent`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The frame's size in bytes, or 0 when `quicPutAck` would refuse these arguments.

</scalar-field>

## quicCryptoOverhead

The bytes a CRYPTO frame's header takes for `length` bytes of data at
`offset`: the type, the offset and the length.

```ts
function quicCryptoOverhead(
  offset: i64,
  length: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="offset" type="i64" required>

The crypto stream offset, in bytes, of the frame's first data byte, up to 2^62 − 1.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many data bytes the frame carries.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The header's size in bytes, not counting the data, which is what a sender subtracts from a
  packet's room to see how much data fits.

</scalar-field>

## quicDatagramSize

The size of the DATAGRAM frame `quicPutDatagram` writes for a payload of
`length` bytes: the type, the Length and the payload. This is the size RFC
9221 §3 holds to `max_datagram_frame_size`.

```ts
function quicDatagramSize(length: i32): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

The payload's size in bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The whole frame's size in bytes.

</scalar-field>

## quicFrameAckEliciting

Whether a frame of `type` asks for an acknowledgement (RFC 9000 §13.2):
every frame but ACK, PADDING and CONNECTION_CLOSE.

```ts
function quicFrameAckEliciting(type: i32): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="type" type="i32" required>

The frame type as `quicParseFrame` answers it.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when a packet holding this frame is ack-eliciting, which is what decides whether the
  peer must acknowledge it promptly.

</scalar-field>

## quicFrameAllowed

Whether a frame of `type` may appear in a packet of `packetType` (RFC 9000
§12.4, Table 3). Initial and Handshake packets carry only PADDING, PING,
ACK, CRYPTO and the transport CONNECTION_CLOSE; a 0-RTT packet anything
but ACK, CRYPTO, NEW_TOKEN, HANDSHAKE_DONE and the retire and response
frames a client cannot have a reason to send yet; a 1-RTT packet anything.

```ts
function quicFrameAllowed(
  type: i32,
  packetType: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="type" type="i32" required>

The frame type as `quicParseFrame` answers it in `QuicFrame.type`, every STREAM type as
  `QUIC_FRAME_STREAM`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="packetType" type="i32" required>

The packet's `QUIC_PACKET_*` type from `nish/net/quic-packet`, `QUIC_PACKET_SHORT`
  for 1-RTT.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when §12.4 permits the frame there; false when it does not permit that frame in that
  packet type, and for a packet type that carries no frames, such as Retry.

</scalar-field>

## quicParseFrame

Reads the frame starting at `payload[at]`, inside `payload[at .. end)`,
into `frame`, which is reset first, and answers 0 or the transport error
the RFC names for the break (see the module header). On 0, `frame.end` is
where the next frame starts; after an error the packet is not to be read
further, and `frame.type` still holds the type when it was read, which is
what CONNECTION_CLOSE reports. A window outside `payload` is
`QUIC_ERROR_INTERNAL`, the caller's fault rather than the peer's.

```ts
function quicParseFrame(
  frame: QuicFrame,
  payload: u8[],
  at: i32,
  end: i32,
): i64
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="frame" type="QuicFrame" required>

The frame to fill, reused across frames and packets; its windows (`dataStart` and the
  like) are offsets into `payload`, so they mean something only while `payload` is unchanged.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="payload" type="u8[]" required>

The decrypted packet payload, as the peer sent it; only read, never kept.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The offset of the frame's first byte, its type.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="end" type="i32" required>

One past the last byte the frame may use, normally the payload's end; a frame reaching past
  it is `QUIC_ERROR_FRAME_ENCODING`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i64">

`QUIC_ERROR_NO_ERROR` (0) for a good frame, otherwise the `QUIC_ERROR_*` code to close the
  connection with.

</scalar-field>

## quicPushAck

Appends the ACK frame `quicPutAck` writes. Answers `false`, appending nothing, where it refuses.

```ts
function quicPushAck(
  out: u8[],
  ranges: i64[],
  rangeCount: i32,
  ackDelay: i64,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to append the frame to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ranges" type="i64[]" required>

Packet number pairs laid out flat, `[smallest, largest]` for each range, highest range first.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="rangeCount" type="i32" required>

How many pairs to read from the front of `ranges`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ackDelay" type="i64" required>

The ACK Delay field, already scaled by this endpoint's `ack_delay_exponent`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the frame was appended.

</scalar-field>

## quicPushConnectionClose

Appends the frame `quicPutConnectionClose` writes. Answers `false`, appending nothing, where it
refuses.

```ts
function quicPushConnectionClose(
  out: u8[],
  application: boolean,
  errorCode: i64,
  frameType: i64,
  reason: u8[],
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to append the frame to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="application" type="boolean" required>

Whether the close is the application's (0x1d) rather than the transport's (0x1c).

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="errorCode" type="i64" required>

A `QUIC_ERROR_*` code for a transport close, the application's own code otherwise.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="frameType" type="i64" required>

The frame type that caused a transport error, 0 when none did; ignored when `application`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="reason" type="u8[]" required>

The whole array is the reason phrase, UTF-8, possibly empty; copied, not kept.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the frame was appended.

</scalar-field>

## quicPushCrypto

Appends the CRYPTO frame `quicPutCrypto` writes. Answers `false`, appending nothing, where it refuses.

```ts
function quicPushCrypto(
  out: u8[],
  offset: i64,
  data: u8[],
  from: i32,
  length: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to append the frame to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="offset" type="i64" required>

The crypto stream offset, in bytes, of the first byte carried.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The handshake bytes to take the window from; copied, not kept.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="from" type="i32" required>

The offset in `data` of the first byte to carry.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many bytes to carry.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the frame was appended.

</scalar-field>

## quicPushNewConnectionId

Appends a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame (§19.15). Answers `false` for a
connection ID outside 1 to 20 bytes, a reset token that is not 16 bytes, a
Retire Prior To above the sequence number, or a value no varint holds.

```ts
function quicPushNewConnectionId(
  out: u8[],
  sequence: i64,
  retirePriorTo: i64,
  connectionId: u8[],
  resetToken: u8[],
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to append the frame to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sequence" type="i64" required>

The sequence number this endpoint gives the new connection ID.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="retirePriorTo" type="i64" required>

The peer is to retire every connection ID of a lower sequence number; 0 retires none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="connectionId" type="u8[]" required>

The new ID, the whole array; copied, not kept.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="resetToken" type="u8[]" required>

The 16-byte stateless reset token tied to the ID; copied, not kept.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the frame was appended; false, appending nothing, otherwise.

</scalar-field>

## quicPushNewToken

Appends a NEW_TOKEN frame (§19.7) carrying `token`. Answers `false` for an
empty token, which §19.7 forbids.

```ts
function quicPushNewToken(
  out: u8[],
  token: u8[],
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to append the frame to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="token" type="u8[]" required>

The whole array is the token the client is to present later; copied, not kept.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the frame was appended; false, appending nothing, for an empty token.

</scalar-field>

## quicPushStream

Appends a STREAM frame (§19.8) carrying `data[from .. from + length)` on
`streamId` at `offset`, with FIN when `fin`, as `quicPutStream` writes it.
Answers `false`, appending nothing, for a window outside `data`, a stream
ID that is not a varint or an end past 2^62 − 1.

```ts
function quicPushStream(
  out: u8[],
  streamId: i64,
  offset: i64,
  data: u8[],
  from: i32,
  length: i32,
  fin: boolean,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to append the frame to.

<scalar-field name="streamId" type="i64" required>

</scalar-field>

The offset in `data` of the first byte to carry.

True when the frame was appended.

</scalar-field>

## quicPutAck

Writes an ACK frame (§19.3) for the `rangeCount` pairs of `ranges`, each
`[smallest, largest]`, from the highest down and not touching (each pair's
largest at least two below the smallest of the pair before it), with
`ackDelay` already scaled by this endpoint's exponent. Answers -1, writing
nothing, where `quicAckSize` answers 0 or the frame does not fit.

```ts
function quicPutAck(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  end: i32,
  ranges: i64[],
  rangeCount: i32,
  ackDelay: i64,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer to write into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The offset of the frame's first byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="end" type="i32" required>

One past the last byte the frame may use.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ranges" type="i64[]" required>

Packet number pairs laid out flat, `[smallest, largest]` for each range, highest range first.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="rangeCount" type="i32" required>

How many pairs to read from the front of `ranges`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ackDelay" type="i64" required>

The ACK Delay field, already scaled: microseconds shifted right by the exponent.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The offset past the frame, or -1 with nothing written. The frame is always type 0x02, without ECN
  counts.

</scalar-field>

## quicPutConnectionClose

Writes a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (§19.19): with `application` false the
transport form 0x1c, carrying `frameType`, the type of the frame that
caused the error (0 when none did); with `application` true the 0x1d form,
which has no frame type. `reason` is the phrase, UTF-8, possibly empty.
Answers -1 for a value no varint holds, or no room.

```ts

  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  end: i32,
  application: boolean,
  errorCode: i64,
  frameType: i64,
  reason: u8[],
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="end" type="i32" required>

One past the last byte the frame may use.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="application" type="boolean" required>

Whether the close is the application's (0x1d) rather than the transport's (0x1c).

</scalar-field>

A `QUIC_ERROR_*` code for a transport close, the application's own code otherwise.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="frameType" type="i64" required>

The frame type that caused a transport error, 0 when none did; ignored when `application`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="reason" type="u8[]" required>

The whole array is the reason phrase; copied, not kept.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The offset past the frame, or -1 with nothing written.

</scalar-field>

## quicPutStream

Writes a STREAM frame (§19.8) carrying `length` bytes of `data` on
`streamId` at `offset`, with FIN when `fin`. The data is read from `data`
as a ring: byte `k` of it is `data[(from + k) % data.length]`, so a
stream's send buffer is framed where it wraps without a copy; a `from`
plus `length` inside the array is the plain window. The Length field is
always written, so another frame may follow; the Offset field only when it
is not zero. Answers -1, writing nothing, for a `length` past the array, a
stream ID that is not a varint, an end past 2^62 − 1, or no room.

```ts
function quicPutStream(
  buf: u8[],
  at: i32,
  end: i32,
  streamId: i64,
  offset: i64,
  data: u8[],
  from: i32,
  length: i32,
  fin: boolean,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="buf" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer to write into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

The offset of the frame's first byte.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="end" type="i32" required>

One past the last byte the frame may use.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="streamId" type="i64" required>

The stream the data belongs to.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="offset" type="i64" required>

The stream offset, in bytes, of the first byte carried.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to carry, read as a ring; copied, not kept.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="from" type="i32" required>

The index in `data` of the first byte to carry, inside the array when `length` is above zero.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many bytes to carry, at most `data.length`; 0 for a frame that only carries FIN.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="fin" type="boolean" required>

Whether these bytes end the stream, so that `offset + length` is its final size.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The offset past the frame, or -1 with nothing written.

</scalar-field>

## QuicFrame

One frame as `quicParseFrame` read it. Which fields mean something depends
on `type`; the rest hold zero, or empty arrays.

- ACK and ACK_ECN: `largest`, `ackDelay` (still scaled by the peer's
  exponent), the ranges as `[smallest, largest]` pairs from the highest
  down in `ackRanges` (`ackRangeCount` pairs stored, `ackRangeTotal` read),
  and for ACK_ECN the counts `ect0`, `ect1` and `ce`.
- CRYPTO: `offset` and the data `dataStart`, `dataLength`.
- STREAM: `streamId`, `offset`, the data, and `fin`.
- NEW_TOKEN and PATH_CHALLENGE / PATH_RESPONSE: the token or data.
- RESET_STREAM: `streamId`, `errorCode`, the final size in `value`.
- STOP_SENDING: `streamId`, `errorCode`.
- MAX_DATA, MAX_STREAMS_*, DATA_BLOCKED, STREAMS_BLOCKED_*: `value`.
- MAX_STREAM_DATA, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED: `streamId` and `value`.
- NEW_CONNECTION_ID: the sequence number in `value`, `retirePriorTo`,
  the ID's window `connectionIdStart` / `connectionIdLength` and the
  reset token's `resetTokenStart` (16 bytes) in the payload.
  RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID: `value`.
- DATAGRAM: the payload as the data, and `fin` when the frame carried a
  Length (type 0x31).
- CONNECTION_CLOSE: `errorCode`, `frameType` (0x1c only) and the reason
  phrase as the data.

```ts
class QuicFrame
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicFrame()` | Makes an empty frame with room for `QUIC_FRAME_MAX_ACK_RANGES` ACK ranges, for `quicParseFrame` to fill. |
| `ackDelay: i64` | An ACK's delay as sent, not yet scaled by the peer's `ack_delay_exponent`. |
| `ackRangeCount: i32` | How many `[smallest, largest]` pairs of `ackRanges` hold an ACK range, at most `QUIC_FRAME_MAX_ACK_RANGES`. |
| `ackRanges: i64[]` | An ACK's ranges as `[smallest, largest]` packet-number pairs, highest first. Only the first `ackRangeCount` pairs are meaningful; the array keeps its `QUIC_FRAME_MAX_ACK_RANGES * 2` length. |
| `ackRangeTotal: i64` | How many ranges the ACK carried, which can exceed `ackRangeCount` when ranges past the stored cap were read and dropped. |
| `ce: i64` | An ACK_ECN's cumulative count of packets received marked ECN-CE (congestion experienced). |
| `connectionIdLength: i32` | A NEW_CONNECTION_ID's connection ID length in bytes, 1 to 20. |
| `connectionIdStart: i32` | Where a NEW_CONNECTION_ID's connection ID starts in the payload. |
| `dataLength: i32` | How many bytes of data start at `dataStart`. |
| `dataStart: i32` | Where the frame's data (stream or CRYPTO bytes, token, path data, datagram or reason phrase) starts in the payload. |
| `ect0: i64` | An ACK_ECN's cumulative count of packets received marked ECT(0). |
| `ect1: i64` | An ACK_ECN's cumulative count of packets received marked ECT(1). |
| `end: i32` | One past the frame's last byte, where the next frame starts. |
| `errorCode: i64` | The application or transport error code of a RESET_STREAM, STOP_SENDING or CONNECTION_CLOSE. |
| `fin: boolean` | A STREAM frame's FIN bit (the stream ends with this data), or a DATAGRAM that carried a Length. |
| `frameType: i64` | The frame type a transport CONNECTION_CLOSE (0x1c) blames; 0 for the application form. |
| `largest: i64` | The largest packet number an ACK acknowledges. |
| `offset: i64` | The byte offset in the stream (STREAM) or the handshake stream (CRYPTO) where the data starts. |
| `resetTokenStart: i32` | Where a NEW_CONNECTION_ID's 16-byte stateless reset token starts in the payload. |
| `retirePriorTo: i64` | A NEW_CONNECTION_ID's Retire Prior To: every peer ID with a lower sequence number is to be retired. |
| `streamId: i64` | The stream a STREAM, RESET_STREAM, STOP_SENDING, MAX_STREAM_DATA or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame names. |
| `type: i32` | The frame type, with every STREAM type answered as `QUIC_FRAME_STREAM`. |
| `value: i64` | The frame's one number: a limit, a final size or a sequence number, as the list above gives per type. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="32" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_MAX_ACK_RANGES: i32`

The most ACK ranges a `QuicFrame` keeps. A frame may list more, and every
one is still checked; the ones past this are counted in `ackRangeTotal`
but not stored. Loss recovery, which would read them, is WP34 Q3.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="0x0f" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_AEAD_LIMIT_REACHED: i64`

AEAD_LIMIT_REACHED: the keys reached their confidentiality or integrity limit (RFC 9001 §6.6).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0c" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_APPLICATION: i64`

APPLICATION_ERROR: the application closed, reported in a transport close where 0x1d may not be sent.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x09" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT: i64`

CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR: the peer gave more connection IDs than `active_connection_id_limit`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x02" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_CONNECTION_REFUSED: i64`

CONNECTION_REFUSED: the server will not accept the connection.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0100" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_CRYPTO: i64`

CRYPTO_ERROR is this plus the TLS alert description (RFC 9001 §4.8): 0x0100 to 0x01ff.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0d" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED: i64`

CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED: the peer sent more CRYPTO data than the endpoint buffers.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x06" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_FINAL_SIZE: i64`

FINAL_SIZE_ERROR: a stream's final size changed, or data arrived past it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x03" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_FLOW_CONTROL: i64`

FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR: the peer sent more data than the advertised limits allow.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x07" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_FRAME_ENCODING: i64`

FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR: a frame is badly formed, such as truncated or with a length past the packet.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x01" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_INTERNAL: i64`

INTERNAL_ERROR: the endpoint broke on its own, not because of anything the peer sent.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0b" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_INVALID_TOKEN: i64`

INVALID_TOKEN: a server received a client Initial whose Token field it cannot accept, from a Retry or NEW_TOKEN.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0e" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_KEY_UPDATE: i64`

KEY_UPDATE_ERROR: the peer made a mistake in a key update (RFC 9001 §6).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x00" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_NO_ERROR: i64`

NO_ERROR: the connection closes without an error; also `quicParseFrame`'s answer for a good frame.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_NO_VIABLE_PATH: i64`

NO_VIABLE_PATH: no network path is fit for QUIC, such as one whose MTU is too small.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x0a" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION: i64`

PROTOCOL_VIOLATION: the peer broke the protocol in a way no more specific code names.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x04" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_STREAM_LIMIT: i64`

STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR: the peer opened a stream past the limit it was given.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x05" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_STREAM_STATE: i64`

STREAM_STATE_ERROR: a frame arrived for a stream not in a state that permits it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x08" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_ERROR_TRANSPORT_PARAMETER: i64`

TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR: the peer's transport parameters are malformed or invalid.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x02" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_ACK: i32`

ACK without ECN counts.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x03" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_ACK_ECN: i32`

ACK with the three ECN counts after the ranges.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x1c" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_CONNECTION_CLOSE: i32`

CONNECTION_CLOSE with a transport error code and the frame type that caused it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x1d" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_CONNECTION_CLOSE_APP: i32`

CONNECTION_CLOSE with an application error code, allowed only in 1-RTT packets.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x06" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_CRYPTO: i32`

CRYPTO (§19.6): TLS handshake bytes at an offset in one packet number space's crypto stream.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x30" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_DATAGRAM: i32`

DATAGRAM (RFC 9221 §4): an unreliable application payload. Type 0x30 runs
to the end of the packet and 0x31 carries a Length; `quicParseFrame`
answers both as this type, with `fin` set for 0x31 (it had a Length).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x31" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_DATAGRAM_LENGTH: i32`

The DATAGRAM type with a Length field (RFC 9221 §4), which `quicPutDatagram` always writes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x14" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_DATA_BLOCKED: i32`

DATA_BLOCKED (§19.12): the sender has data to send but the connection limit holds it back.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x1e" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_HANDSHAKE_DONE: i32`

HANDSHAKE_DONE (§19.20): the server confirms the handshake; only a server sends it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_MAX_DATA: i32`

MAX_DATA (§19.9): the connection's flow-control limit, in bytes across every stream.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x12" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_MAX_STREAMS_BIDI: i32`

MAX_STREAMS (§19.11) for bidirectional streams: how many the peer may open in all.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x13" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_MAX_STREAMS_UNI: i32`

MAX_STREAMS (§19.11) for unidirectional streams: how many the peer may open in all.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_MAX_STREAM_DATA: i32`

MAX_STREAM_DATA (§19.10): one stream's flow-control limit, in bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x18" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_NEW_CONNECTION_ID: i32`

NEW_CONNECTION_ID (§19.15): another connection ID the peer may use, with its reset token.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x07" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_NEW_TOKEN: i32`

NEW_TOKEN (§19.7): a server's token for the client to present in a later connection's Initial.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x00" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_PADDING: i32`

PADDING (§19.1): a single zero byte that means nothing, used to make a packet bigger.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x1a" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_PATH_CHALLENGE: i32`

PATH_CHALLENGE (§19.17): eight bytes the peer must echo in a PATH_RESPONSE to validate a path.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x1b" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_PATH_RESPONSE: i32`

PATH_RESPONSE (§19.18): the eight bytes of a PATH_CHALLENGE, echoed back.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x01" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_PING: i32`

PING (§19.2): the type alone, sent to get an acknowledgement or to keep a connection alive.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x04" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_RESET_STREAM: i32`

RESET_STREAM (§19.4): the sender abandons a stream, with an error code and the final size.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x19" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID: i32`

RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID (§19.16): the sender stops using the peer's connection ID of a sequence number.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x05" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_STOP_SENDING: i32`

STOP_SENDING (§19.5): asks the peer to stop sending on a stream, with an error code.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x08" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_STREAM: i32`

The first of the eight STREAM types, 0x08 to 0x0f. `quicParseFrame` answers
every one of them as this type, with the three low bits read into
`offset`, `dataLength` and `fin` (§19.8).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_STREAMS_BLOCKED_BIDI: i32`

STREAMS_BLOCKED (§19.14) for bidirectional streams: the sender wants to open more than it may.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x17" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_STREAMS_BLOCKED_UNI: i32`

STREAMS_BLOCKED (§19.14) for unidirectional streams: the sender wants to open more than it may.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0x15" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_FRAME_STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED: i32`

STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED (§19.13): the sender is held back by one stream's limit.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_PATH_DATA_SIZE: i32`

The length of a PATH_CHALLENGE's and a PATH_RESPONSE's data (RFC 9000 §19.17).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RESET_TOKEN_SIZE: i32`

The length of a stateless reset token (RFC 9000 §10.3).

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
